```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

A design-based structural equation model takes a lavaan model and a survey design. Sampling weights, strata, and primary sampling units enter the variance. The point estimates are the weighted estimates.

```{r setup}
library(svysem)
design <- simulate_design(n_psu = 6, n_per = 4, n_strata = 2, seed = 1)
```

## Estimators

`estimator = "MLM"` is maximum likelihood with a Satorra-Bentler adjustment. It is for complete continuous data. A regression with a mean structure and free covariates matches the design used by `survey::svyglm()`.

```{r mlm}
regression <- svysem(
  "y ~ x1 + x2", design,
  fixed.x = FALSE, meanstructure = TRUE
)
coef(regression)
```

`estimator = "MLR"` is robust maximum likelihood with a Yuan-Bentler adjustment. `missing = "ml"` scores each row on the indicators that row observed. The sampling weight of an incomplete row stays in the design.

```{r mlr}
incomplete <- design
incomplete$variables$y2[c(1, 8, 15)] <- NA
mlr <- svycfa(
  "f =~ y1 + y2 + y3 + y4", incomplete,
  estimator = "MLR", missing = "ml"
)
mlr@estimator
lavaan::lavInspect(mlr, "nobs")
```

`estimator = "WLSMV"` is for ordered indicators. The point estimates use lavaan's weighted diagonally weighted least squares matrix. The standard errors use replicate weights. With strata, the default replicate type is a stratified jackknife.

```{r wlsmv}
frame <- design$variables
frame$a <- ordered(findInterval(frame$y1, c(-0.5, 0.5)))
frame$b <- ordered(findInterval(frame$y2, c(0)))
frame$c <- ordered(findInterval(frame$y3, c(-0.4, 0.6)))
ordinal <- survey::svydesign(
  ids = ~psu, strata = ~strat, weights = ~w, data = frame
)
ordered_fit <- svycfa(
  "f =~ a + b + c", ordinal,
  estimator = "WLSMV", ordered = c("a", "b", "c")
)
ordered_fit@variance_method
```

## Domains and replicate-weight designs

`subset()` keeps the primary sampling units of the full design, which is the variance for a domain. A design that already carries replicate weights is used as it stands. `variance_method` is then `"replication"` for every estimator.

```{r domain}
domain <- subset(design, strat == 1)
domain_fit <- svysem(
  "y ~ x1", domain, fixed.x = FALSE, meanstructure = TRUE
)
domain_fit@df

replicated <- survey::as.svrepdesign(design, type = "auto")
rep_fit <- svycfa("f =~ y1 + y2 + y3 + y4", replicated, estimator = "MLR")
rep_fit@variance_method
```

## Factor scores

`predict()` returns posterior means for continuous outcomes. `lavaan::lavPredict()` on a weighted fit returns a different number. Draws from the posterior, when requested, are plausible values for one completed data set.

```{r scores}
predict(mlr)[1, , drop = FALSE]
```
